motion_rule: the yard slides past her without a pause. She never works a prop in place: she rides, hauls, throws. The camera tracks her and changes shot size every beat, never wider than a mid shot, her body filling half the frame. Movement runs across frame, never into depth or straight up. Laundry and windows stream past every beat.
character: a slim grey turtle dove, pink breast, black neck ring, head stabbing the air
second_characters: ONE sparrow working at the lens: rides past on a peg, snaps at her, never still
props: ONE rolled banknote pegged among the sheets, sliding with them; ONE wooden peg carriage she rides
prop_continuity: the banknote slides past her from 1.40 on, closer every beat, ripped off by the wind at 7.45
environment: a courtyard packed wall to wall with washing lines, sheets, balconies, windows, pigeons on every ledge
light_events: hard midday sun, sharp shadows racing across the white sheets

audio.language: Russian, lines verbatim; latin hints never spoken
audio.delivery: soft cooing female voice gone hard, preaching, biting each word, 4 syllables/sec
audio.pronunciation: ot-LO-zhish, CHOR-ny, pri-DYOT, CHOR-na-ya, DEN-gi, spa-SUT, TOL-ko, KRY-lya
audio.pacing: 0.00-1.75, 2.25-3.75 and 4.60-6.85 each one breath; after 6.85 not a word, sfx keep going
audio.lip_sync: her beak opens wide and shapes every syllable, throat swelling
audio.sfx: wind, sheets cracking, the peg carriage squealing, pegs snapping off

timeline.a: she runs the sagging wire, knocking pegs off with her beak, a wet sheet sweeping past behind
she hops on the peg carriage and it runs off down the wire, past window after window
the banknote slides the other way past her nose; she snaps at it and misses
the sparrow shoots past the lens on his own peg, the wire whips, she rides on
riding hard, she rears up and stabs her beak at the yard, a pillowcase banging past
the carriage hits a knot and throws her forward; she preaches on mid stumble
she snaps her head to profile as a bedsheet wipes across the frame behind her
she kicks the carriage at the sparrow, both tumble across frame, she catches the wire
she hauls herself along the wire toe over toe, the yard sliding by
she runs the top line at full stride, throat swollen, the sparrow racing her below
she drives through a row of pegs, they fly off, a sheet drops behind her
she rises on her toes at full stride, wings half up, the banknote sliding in close
she throws both wings wide and pushes off the wire, pegs scattering under her
she flies flat across the yard, sheets tearing past her wingtips
the wind rips the banknote off its peg at the lens; her head whips round after it
she dives into the lens after it, wings beating hard, pegs blowing past
the note slaps across her face; her beak snaps at it, both feet tearing at the air
blinded, she ploughs on across frame, snapping, as the washing line comes down behind

must_appear: she rides the peg carriage down the wire while preaching; the banknote hangs pegged among the laundry; at 8.20 she lunges into the lens after it, beak snapping
negative_prompt: subtitles, watermark, letterbox, a horizontal 16:9 frame, blurred bands, a wide shot, a parked camera, a bird working a prop in place, a closed beak while speaking, a bird flying straight up, slow motion, a foreign accent, a word not in the lines, cyrillic letters, words
